record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: How robust is AIXI to observations that contain irrelevant information, especially when that irrelevant input is complex or non-computable rather than computably generated noise, and under what conditions can AIXI separate such irrelevant input from the information relevant for future observations and rewards?

evidence.quote: i) Relevant and non-computable environments µ. Assume that the observations of AIXI contain irrelevant information, like noise. ... More interesting is the case, where the irrelevant input is complex. If it is easily separable from the useful input it should not affect AIXI. ... How robustly does AIXI deal with complex but irrelevant inputs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{O}$ and $\mathcal{R}\subseteq[0,1]$ be finite sets of observations and rewards, and let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set of actions. Write $\mathcal{X}=\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{R}$ for percepts. An environment is a probability measure $\mu$ on infinite interaction histories $a_1 x_1 a_2 x_2 \dots \in (\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{X})^\infty$, specifying for every history the conditional distribution $\mu(x_t\mid a_1 x_1\cdots a_{t-1} x_{t-1} a_t)$ over the next percept. The agent AIXI is defined, with horizon discount and a universal lower-semicomputable semimeasure $\xi$ (Solomonoff's universal mixture over all lower-semicomputable chronological semimeasures), as the policy
$$ a_t^{\mathrm{AIXI}} = \arg\max_{a_t}\sum_{x_t}\max_{a_{t+1}}\sum_{x_{t+1}}\cdots \Big(\sum_{k=t}^{\infty}\gamma_k r_k\Big)\,\xi(x_t x_{t+1}\cdots\mid a_1 x_1\cdots a_t a_{t+1}\cdots),$$
for some bounded discount sequence $\gamma_k \geq 0$ with $\sum_k \gamma_k < \infty$.

Decompose each observation as $o_t = (u_t, v_t)\in\mathcal{U}\times\mathcal{V}$, where $u_t$ is the "useful" component and $v_t$ is an "irrelevant" component, in the precise sense that the conditional distribution
$$\mu(u_{t+1}, r_{t+1}\mid a_1 x_1\cdots a_t x_t a_{t+1}) = \mu(u_{t+1}, r_{t+1}\mid a_1 u_1 r_1\cdots a_t u_t r_t a_{t+1})$$
depends only on the past useful components and rewards (so $v_{1:t}$ carries no information about future $u$'s and $r$'s given past $u$'s and $r$'s). Assume the marginal process $(v_t)_{t\ge 1}$ is generated independently (or independently conditioned on the agent's actions) from a source $\nu$.

Question. Establish, or refute by counterexample, the following form of robustness of AIXI:

(a) If $\nu$ is a computable (lower-semicomputable) source — i.e., $(v_t)$ is computably generated noise — show that the asymptotic value attained by AIXI on $\mu$ equals the asymptotic value of AIXI on the marginalized environment $\mu_{\mathcal U,\mathcal R}$ obtained by removing the $v$-component (i.e., AIXI's policy and expected discounted reward are unaffected, in the limit, by the presence of $v_{1:\infty}$).

(b) More generally, allow $\nu$ to be a non-computable / Kolmogorov-complex source for $(v_t)$. Identify necessary and sufficient conditions on $\nu$, on the encoding of $(u_t, v_t)$ into $o_t$, and on the discount sequence $(\gamma_k)$ under which AIXI's behavior and value remain (asymptotically) invariant under replacement of $\mu$ by $\mu_{\mathcal U,\mathcal R}$. In particular, determine whether complexity of $v$ alone can cause AIXI to suffer arbitrarily large value loss compared with the optimal policy on $\mu$, and characterize the cases in which AIXI provably "separates" the irrelevant input $v$ from the relevant signal $(u, r)$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published result establishes general robustness of AIXI to complex or non-computable but irrelevant components of observations. Discussions of AIXI's optimality (e.g., embedded-agency surveys) note that even basic optimality results for AIXI require strong realizability/computability assumptions on the environment, and the question of separating irrelevant non-computable inputs from relevant signals does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Embedded Agency (Demski & Garrabrant)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion noting that AIXI's optimality results require a realizability assumption and that its behavior under more general environments is not well understood.
status_evidence.claim: AIXI's robustness/optimality outside computable-environment assumptions is not established.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists robustness of AIXI to complex/non-computable irrelevant inputs as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is posed as open in the universal-induction open-problems literature.
